body.working_title: Admissibility of lagged SSOE models: replacing the per-lag eigenvalue check

body.text: Which criterion decides whether a pure additive lagged SSOE model (ADAM notation, components with different lags, including GUM) forgets its initial states, and how can it be computed efficiently inside the estimation loop?

Before this record was started, the agent ran unrecorded numpy checks (in a scratchpad, not in the repository) while designing the checker for issue openforecast-org/smooth#415 with the human. Those checks shaped the criterion and the hypotheses below. Their code was consolidated into .claude/research/eigenChecker and is re-run here as exploratory run(s), so that every number used later comes from a recorded run.

Prototype in numpy before the R/C++ implementation: the criterion is the invertibility of the MA polynomial theta(B) = det(I - D L(B)) of the model's ARIMA form, after cancelling the cyclotomic factors it shares with phi(B) = det(I - F L(B)), with coefficients from an inverse DFT and the decision from the step-down (Schur-Cohn) recursion.

body.statement: The per-lag eigenvalue check of smoothEigens() (eigenvalues of the diagonal blocks of D = F - g w', one block per lag) accepts lagged SSOE models that do not forget their initial states (some controllable and observable mode of the expanded discount matrix has |lambda| > 1): ETS(A,N,A) models with m = 4 or 12 on a grid of alpha and gamma in (0, 2), and GUM models with lags (1, 12) and random F, g, w.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: The per-lag eigenvalue check of smoothEigens() rejects some GUM models with lags (1, 12) that do forget their initial states (every controllable and observable mode of the expanded discount matrix has |lambda| < 1).
body.question: Q1

body.statement: For additive ETS models (level, optional damped trend, up to two seasonal lags, optional constant, some persistence fixed at zero) and GUM models (identity or random transition), dividing theta(B) = det(I - D L(B)) and phi(B) = det(I - F L(B)) by the cyclotomic factors Phi_n (n dividing a lag) they share gives the same admissibility decision as the controllable and observable modes of the expanded discount matrix (PBH reference), and the same max |lambda| within 1e-6 on inadmissible models.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: The step-down (Schur-Cohn) recursion applied to the cancelled MA polynomial theta*(B) gives the same admissibility decision as the roots of theta*, for ETS and GUM models with polynomial degrees up to 366.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: For inadmissible models, bisection on r with the step-down test applied to theta*(B/r) gives max |lambda| within 1e-8 of the value from the roots of theta*.
body.question: Q1

body.design: python3 .claude/research/eigenChecker/confirm.py --test perlag --seed 2026 --n 200 at the committed code: ETS(A,N,A) with m in {4, 12}, alpha and gamma on the grid 0.05, 0.10, ..., 1.95 (3042 models), and 200 GUM models with lags (1, 12), F ~ N(0, 0.35), g ~ N(0, 0.175), w ~ N(1, 0.175). Seed 2026 has not been used before.
body.analysis: For each model: per-lag max |lambda| (diagonal blocks of D by lag) and the PBH reference (max |lambda| over the controllable and observable modes of the expanded discount matrix, rank tolerance 1e-7 relative). Count, per family, models with per-lag max < 1 and reference > 1 + 1e-8.

ets_bad.quantity: models accepted by the per-lag check that do not forget their initial states

body.analysis: For each GUM model: per-lag max |lambda| and the PBH reference. Count models with per-lag max >= 1 and reference < 1 - 1e-8.

parameters.sample: 200 random GUM models, fixed; no interim analysis

gum_rej.quantity: models rejected by the per-lag check that forget their initial states

body.design: python3 .claude/research/eigenChecker/confirm.py --test cancel --seed 2026 --n 200 at the committed code: 200 random additive ETS models (level; trend none, additive or damped with phi in (0.8, 0.99); 0-2 seasonal lags from {4, 7, 12, 24, 52}; constant with probability 0.3; beta = 0 with probability 0.1 and each gamma = 0 with probability 0.15), 100 GUM models with F = I and random lags from {1, 4, 12}, g ~ U(-0.3, 0.6), w ~ N(1, 0.3), and 200 random GUM models with lags from {1, 4, 12, 24}, F ~ N(0, 0.35).
body.analysis: theta and phi by inverse DFT, divided by the shared cyclotomic factors (remainder tolerance 1e-9 relative); max |lambda| from the roots of the cancelled theta against the PBH reference. Models with reference within 1e-8 of 1 are excluded. Count the differing decisions; max abs difference of max |lambda| over models both methods find inadmissible.

mism.quantity: admissibility decisions that differ from the PBH reference

diff.quantity: max abs difference of max |lambda| from the PBH reference, inadmissible models

body.design: python3 .claude/research/eigenChecker/confirm.py --test stepdown --seed 2026 --n 200 at the committed code: the 500 models of the plan for H3 generated afresh from seed 2026, plus 50 ETS models with seasonal lags from {24, 168, 365} and 25 GUM models with lags (1, 24, 168), F ~ N(0, 0.3) (degrees up to 366 before cancellation).
body.analysis: Cancelled theta as for H3; the step-down decision against the decision from numpy's roots of the cancelled theta. Models with root-based max |lambda| within 1e-8 of 1 are excluded. Count the differing decisions.

mism.quantity: step-down decisions that differ from the decision by the roots

body.design: python3 .claude/research/eigenChecker/confirm.py --test bisection --seed 2026 --n 200 at the committed code: the 575 models of the plan for H4.
body.analysis: For every model whose cancelled theta has a root-based max |lambda| > 1 + 1e-8: bisection on r in [1, 2^j] to width 1e-10 with the step-down test on theta*(B/r), against the root-based value. Max abs difference.

parameters.sample: the inadmissible models among 575, fixed; no interim analysis

diff.quantity: max abs difference of max |lambda|, bisection against roots

body.rationale: Rule of PL1 met: ets_bad = 1482 > 0 and gum_bad = 10 > 0.
Rule of PL3 met: no differing decision on 500 models and max difference 4.4e-13 < 1e-6.
Rule of PL4 met: no differing decision on 575 models.
Rule of PL5 met: max difference 5.8e-11 < 1e-8 over 198 inadmissible models.

body.text: The ETS(A,N,A) part of PL1 uses a fixed grid of alpha and gamma that does not depend on the seed, so it is the same grid as exploratory run RN3, whose result prompted H1. Only the GUM part of PL1 (200 models from seed 2026) is new data. For the ETS part the confirmatory run repeats a deterministic computation rather than testing on new data.

The PBH reference (pbh_max) and the cyclotomic cancellation share the lag-1 expansion code (expand) and the numpy/LAPACK eigenvalue routines, and were written by the same agent; the agreement in PL3 is not a check by an independent implementation.

Exploratory timings (RN2, numpy, one machine, degree 193): coefficients by inverse DFT 4.7 ms with a Python loop over 256 points, step-down test 0.007 ms, all roots by numpy companion eigenvalues 22 ms.

body.description: numpy prototype of the admissibility check of pure additive lagged SSOE models: lag-1 expansion, the per-lag check of smoothEigens(), the PBH reference, ARIMA-form polynomials by inverse DFT, cyclotomic cancellation, step-down test and bisection; ETS and GUM model builders
exploratory script: ETS(A,N,A) cases, multiple seasonality and the GUM starting point, determinant identity, step-down and bisection on random GUMs, timings
test script: per-lag check against the PBH reference, cancellation against the PBH reference, step-down decisions and bisection against roots, on seeded random model sets
